page: Amazon Web Services c7i.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by a 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor built on x86_64 architecture, providing 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 96 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, establishing a 2 GB per core ratio. The CPU incorporates 105 MB of L3 cache and supports specialized instruction sets, including AVX-512, Intel AMX tile and int8 extensions, and SHA-NI cryptography acceleration. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or discrete GPUs, relying on external storage over a 19 Gbps baseline network connection.

Benchmark evaluations show high computational and instruction throughput. The instance ranks in the upper quartile for Geekbench single-core (2074.0) and multi-core (17515.0) scores, as well as software compilation via Clang (41626.0). Memory benchmarks demonstrate high read throughput, measuring 3865.15 GB/s on small-block cached transfers and 203.15 GB/s on large-block uncached reads. Extended instruction tests in PassMark achieved 59981.53, complemented by strong results in static web serving at 68.7 GB/s and text generation on small to medium language models. Conversely, large-block memory writes and multi-core stress-ng tests placed in the median bracket.

With its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and lack of local NVMe storage, this instance prioritizes core density over data caching capacity. Workloads requiring large in-memory footprints or high-speed ephemeral local drives will face constraints. It is technically appropriate for distributed CI/CD build environments, compute-bound batch processing, static web fleets, and CPU-based model inference utilizing AMX extensions.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.12xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor operating at 3.2 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores, supported by 105 MB of L3 cache, advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX, and 96 GB of DDR5 system memory running at 5 GHz. With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation, the hardware targets high-compute environments. Networking delivers a 19 Gbps baseline, and the server includes zero local storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate strong results in Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations, Clang compilation, and cached memory reads, alongside high throughput in static web serving and medium-scale LLM CPU inference. The absence of local disk requires external volume attachments, making this instance best fitted for distributed compilation, computational batch processing, static web serving fleets, and CPU-accelerated mathematical pipelines.
